description: Composite two-panel figure pairing an inclusion-population bar chart with an inclusion-density/property scatter plot. (a) Vertical bar chart, y-axis "Percentage of Inclusions" (0-30, gridlines every 5), x-axis listing inclusion types: Al-Mn-S-O, Al2O3, AlN, AlN-MnO, AlN-MnS, pores, Mn-AlO, MnO, MnS, Mn-Si-O, Other nitrides, Other oxides, oxi-sulfides. AlN is by far the tallest bar (above the 25 gridline), then pores (~17), Mn-AlO (~14), AlN-MnO (~12), MnO (~7), oxi-sulfides (~6); Al-Mn-S-O, Other nitrides and Mn-Si-O are the smallest (~2-3). (b) Scatter plot with vertical error bars: y-axis "CVN Energy, Joules" (10-50), x-axis "AlN Density, particles/mm2" (0-60). Legend: Heat 1: base (filled circle), Heat 2: Ca (filled triangle), Heat 3: Ca, Ce (filled square), Heat 4: Ca, Ce, Ar (filled diamond), Heat 5: Ca, Ce, Ar, teapot (light blue circle), Industrial Heat (light blue triangle). CVN energy decreases as AlN density increases: base ~27 J near 30 particles/mm2 falling to ~19 J for Ca, Ce, Ar near 50 particles/mm2, while the two low-AlN-density heats (light blue symbols, near 4-5 particles/mm2) sit highest at ~38-39 J with the widest error bars. Together the panels argue that AlN dominates the inclusion population and that reducing AlN density raises impact energy.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a bar chart of inclusion types whose y-axis is labelled 'Percentage of Inclusions' and runs 0-30 with gridlines every 5.
In panel (a) the AlN bar is the tallest, extending above the 25 gridline, and the next largest fractions are pores (~17%), Mn-AlO (~14%) and AlN-MnO (~12%).

Panel (a) contains 13 inclusion categories labelled Al-Mn-S-O, Al2O3, AlN, AlN-MnO, AlN-MnS, pores, Mn-AlO, MnO, MnS, Mn-Si-O, Other nitrides, Other oxides and oxi-sulfides; Al-Mn-S-O, Other nitrides and Mn-Si-O are the smallest bars, around 2-3%.
Panel (b) plots CVN Energy, Joules (y-axis, 10-50) against AlN Density, particles/mm2 (x-axis, 0-60), all points carrying vertical error bars.

Panel (b) legend lists six conditions: 'Heat 1: base' (filled circle), 'Heat 2: Ca' (filled triangle), 'Heat 3: Ca, Ce' (filled square), 'Heat 4: Ca, Ce, Ar' (filled diamond), 'Heat 5: Ca, Ce, Ar, teapot' (light blue circle) and 'Industrial Heat' (light blue triangle).
In panel (b), CVN energy decreases as AlN density increases: Heat 1 base sits near 30 particles/mm2 at about 27 J and Heat 4 (Ca, Ce, Ar) near 50 particles/mm2 at about 19 J.

In panel (b) the two light-blue symbols, 'Heat 5: Ca, Ce, Ar, teapot' and 'Industrial Heat', lie at the lowest AlN densities (about 4-5 particles/mm2) and at the highest CVN energies (about 38-39 J), with the largest error bars on the plot.
The caption states that (a) is an inclusion analysis of a 0.001% P alloy that was calcium treated and argon stirred and shows a high percentage of AlN.
The caption text supplied for panel (b) is truncated ('A high AlN ...'), so the full claim the caption makes about panel (b) cannot be recovered.
The citing text states that AlN inclusion density was the microstructural parameter showing the greatest correlation to the -40 C CVN impact energy in these calcium and misch metal treated steels.
The citing text states that argon stirring after Ca and misch metal treatment removes AlN inclusions and improves notch toughness, as shown in Fig. 10.

The citing text reports impact energy rising from 33 J in the untreated condition to 108 J with calcium and misch metal additions followed by argon stirring; these values are not printed in either panel.

The caption attributes panel (a) to a calcium-treated, argon-stirred alloy yet the panel shows AlN as the dominant inclusion, whereas the citing sentence says argon stirring removes AlN inclusions; the caption does not specify which heat of panel (b), if any, panel (a) corresponds to.

subfigures.description: Bar chart of inclusion-type distribution: y-axis 'Percentage of Inclusions' (0-30), 13 categorical x-axis labels (Al-Mn-S-O, Al2O3, AlN, AlN-MnO, AlN-MnS, pores, Mn-AlO, MnO, MnS, Mn-Si-O, Other nitrides, Other oxides, oxi-sulfides). AlN is the largest fraction (above 25%), followed by pores (~17%), Mn-AlO (~14%) and AlN-MnO (~12%); the remaining categories are below ~7%.

Scatter plot of CVN Energy, Joules (y, 10-50) versus AlN Density, particles/mm2 (x, 0-60) for six labelled heats (Heat 1: base; Heat 2: Ca; Heat 3: Ca, Ce; Heat 4: Ca, Ce, Ar; Heat 5: Ca, Ce, Ar, teapot; Industrial Heat), each with vertical error bars. Points fall from ~27 J at ~30 particles/mm2 (base) to ~19 J at ~50 particles/mm2 (Ca, Ce, Ar); the two teapot/industrial heats at ~4-5 particles/mm2 give ~38-39 J.
